contradictions.existingQuote: A minimal grade point average (GPA) of 2.75 overall or 3.0 on the last two years of undergraduate work.
contradictions.note: Department admissions page (f22) allows 2.75 overall or 3.0 on the last two years. The catalog's Department Admission Requirements line is 'A minimum GPA of 3.00.' The same catalog page also states the Graduate College 2.75 / 3.00-last-60-credits rule (new fact f64). No winner chosen.

contradictions.existingDetail: A GPA of 3.0 or higher must be maintained; below that, probation, then possible drop if it stays below 3.0 the next regular semester.
contradictions.note: Existing f10 detail used a one-semester window ('the next regular semester'). The 2026-2027 catalog says the student must have an overall GPA of at least 3.00 by the end of two subsequent semesters. No winner chosen.

contradictions.existingQuote: At least 18 credits of computer science courses must be at the 700 level.
contradictions.note: The official 2026-2027 catalog does not repeat this blanket 18-credit rule. It sets subplan-specific minima: 12 credits of 700-level CS excluding thesis (thesis and Integrated BS-MS); 15 credits of 700-level CS excluding the project (project subplan); and 18 credits of 700-level CS (exam subplans). f7 may still be compatible if CS 791 (6) or CS 790 (3) count toward its 18-credit CS 700-level total. No winner chosen.

facts.name: 2026-2027 catalog program title
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 Graduate Catalog program page title is Master of Science in Computer Science. This is the catalog URL that could not be fetched earlier because of an AWS WAF block.
facts.quote: 2026-2027 Graduate Catalog Master of Science in Computer Science

facts.name: Graduate College admission GPA (catalog)
facts.detail: On this 2026-2027 catalog program page, the Graduate College admission requirements ask for a minimum overall GPA of 2.75 for the bachelor's degree, or a minimum 3.00 for the last two years (60 semester credits). This is close to department-admissions-page fact f22 (2.75 overall or 3.0 on the last two years). The same catalog page also has a stricter department line (fact f66).
facts.quote: You must have a minimum overall grade point average of 2.75 (4.00=A) for the bachelor's degree or a minimum 3.00 (4.00=A) for the last two years (60 semester credits).

facts.name: Integrated BS/MS: dual-count graduate courses
facts.detail: The Integrated BS/MS subplan lets high-achieving UNLV CS undergraduates take up to three graduate-level CS courses that can count toward both the B.S. and M.S. programs.
facts.quote: The Integrated BS/MS subplan is designed to provide high-achieving UNLV CS undergraduate students with opportunity to take up to three graduate level CS courses that can count towards both BS and MS degree programs at UNLV.

facts.name: Department catalog GPA minimum 3.00
facts.detail: The Department Admission Requirements on the 2026-2027 catalog program page say applicants must submit a minimum GPA of 3.00. This is stricter than, and conflicts with, existing department-admissions-page fact f22, which quotes a minimal GPA of 2.75 overall or 3.0 on the last two years of undergraduate work. The same catalog page also states the Graduate College 2.75 / 3.00-last-60-credits rule (fact f64). Both catalog lines and f22 are kept; no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: A minimum GPA of 3.00.

facts.name: GRE preferred minimum 297, five-year currency, BS-MS waiver
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 catalog program page requires GRE results current to within five years, sent directly to the department, with a preferred minimum score of 297, and waives the GRE for the Integrated BS-MS subplan. Existing department-admissions-page fact f25 already said GRE results are required but had no numeric cutoff, because this catalog page could not be fetched then. This catalog wording adds the preferred 297 figure, the five-year limit, and the BS-MS waiver; it does not state a hard cutoff. Both facts are kept.
facts.quote: The results of the Graduate Record Examination current to within five years should be sent directly to the department. The preferred minimum score requirement is 297. The GRE requirement is waived for students participating in the Integrated BS-MS subplan.

facts.name: Named undergraduate background courses
facts.detail: The catalog names the expected undergraduate background, with an average grade of B or better: Programming Languages (CS 326), Operating Systems (CS 370), Discrete Mathematics II (MATH 351), and Statistical Methods I (STAT 411). This is more specific than existing department-admissions-page fact f23, which referred only to 'courses equivalent to our basic undergraduate courses.'
facts.quote: In addition, applicants must have completed courses and their prerequisites equivalent to our undergraduate Programming Languages (CS 326), Operating Systems (CS 370), Discrete Mathematics II (MATH 351), and Statistical Methods I (STAT 411) with an average grade of B or better.

facts.name: Conditional admission if background is incomplete
facts.detail: The Computer Science Admission Committee may admit an outstanding applicant who has not satisfied all background requirements on a conditional basis; those requirements must be completed before full admission is granted.
facts.quote: The Computer Science Admission Committee may elect to admit an outstanding applicant who has not satisfied all of the background requirements on a conditional basis.

facts.name: CS 656, 660, and 677 as an admission condition
facts.detail: Students who have not completed CS 656 Automata and Formal Languages, CS 677 Analysis of Algorithms, and CS 660 Compiler Construction (or equivalents) as part of the bachelor's degree may be required to complete them as a condition of admission; if taken in the master's program, they may count toward the 30 credits required. Existing department-master's-page fact f8 instead says that if equivalent courses have not been taken previously, CS 656, 660, and 677 must be included. The catalog frames this as an admission condition rather than a blanket degree-inclusion rule. Both wordings are kept; no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Students who have not completed all the following courses (or equivalent courses) as part of their bachelor's degree may be required to complete them as a condition of their admission. If taken as part of their master's degree program, these courses may count toward the 30 credits required.
facts.note: Wording difference with f8 (admission condition vs 'must be included' in the degree), not treated as a hard contradiction.

facts.name: Integrated BS-MS: nine senior-year credits may be waived
facts.detail: Up to nine credits of approved graduate-level coursework taken as technical electives for a grade of B or better during the senior year will be waived for the graduate degree.
facts.quote: Up to nine credits of approved graduate-level course work can be taken as technical electives for the grade of B or better during the senior year and those credits will be waived for the graduate degree.

facts.name: Integrated BS-MS eligibility and thesis-only rule
facts.detail: To enroll in the Integrated BS-MS program, a student needs at least two semesters of full-time enrollment in the B.S. in Computer Science, normally applies with two semesters remaining in the senior year, and must have completed at least 90 credits applicable to that B.S. with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher. Students have to choose the thesis option, and should request a nomination letter from a Computer Science faculty member and submit it with a short resume (no more than two pages) to the department as well as apply through the Grad Rebel Gateway.
facts.quote: A minimum of 90 credits of course work applicable to the B.S. of Computer Science degree with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher must be completed before beginning the joint degree program.

facts.name: Integrated BS-MS must use the thesis option
facts.detail: Students in the Integrated BS-MS program have to choose the thesis option in the M.S. degree.
facts.quote: Students have to choose the thesis option in the MS degree.

facts.name: Thesis subplan credit split (catalog)
facts.detail: Thesis subplan (Subplan 1): total 30 credits, including 24 credits of 600- or 700-level Computer Science courses (students may complete up to 3 credits outside of CS, related to the research area and approved by the department graduate committee) plus 6 credits of CS 791 Thesis. This agrees with existing 2026-27 thesis plan-of-study facts f11 and f13.
facts.quote: Complete 24 credits of 600- or 700- level Computer Science (CS) courses. Students may complete up to 3 credits outside of CS.

facts.name: Thesis and Integrated BS-MS: 12 credits of 700-level CS excluding thesis
facts.detail: For the Thesis subplan and the Integrated BS-MS subplan, the 2026-2027 catalog says students must complete 12 credits of 700-level CS courses (excluding thesis). This is the official catalog wording that bears on the open 700-level hold. Existing department-page fact f7 says at least 18 credits of computer science courses must be at the 700 level (and does not say 'excluding thesis'). Existing plan-of-study fact f16 says a minimum of 50 percent of the degree program must be 700-level courses, excluding thesis, dissertation, or professional/scholarly paper. Twelve credits excluding a 6-credit thesis is 50 percent of the remaining 24 credits, so f16 is compatible with this catalog line. Whether f7 is compatible depends on whether the 6 credits of CS 791 Thesis count toward that 18-credit CS 700-level total (12 + 6 = 18). The catalog does not restate f7's blanket 18-credit rule and does not use f16's '50 percent' wording. All three are kept; no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Students must complete 12 credits of 700-level CS courses (excluding thesis).
facts.note: Possible contradiction with f7 unless CS 791 thesis credits count toward f7's 18-credit 700-level CS total. Compatible with f16's 50-percent-excluding-thesis rule.

facts.name: Project subplan credit split (catalog)
facts.detail: Project subplan (Subplan 2): total 30 credits, including 27 credits of 600- or 700-level Computer Science courses (up to 3 credits outside of CS, related to the research area and approved by the department graduate committee) plus 3 credits of CS 790 Master's Project. This agrees with existing 2026-27 project plan-of-study fact f14.
facts.quote: Complete 27 credits of 600- or 700- level Computer Science (CS) courses. Students may complete up to 3 credits outside of CS.

facts.name: Project subplan: 15 credits of 700-level CS excluding the project
facts.detail: For the Project subplan, the 2026-2027 catalog says students must complete 15 credits of 700-level CS courses (excluding the project). This also bears on the open 700-level hold. Fifteen credits excluding a 3-credit project meets f16's 50-percent-excluding-project reading (15 of the remaining 27). Compatibility with f7's 18-credit 700-level CS rule depends on whether CS 790 Master's Project credits count toward that 18 (15 + 3 = 18). The catalog does not restate f7 or f16 in those words. All three are kept; no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Students must complete 15 credits of 700-level CS courses (excluding the project).
facts.note: Possible contradiction with f7 unless CS 790 project credits count toward f7's 18-credit 700-level CS total. Compatible with f16.

facts.name: Exam subplans: 18 credits of 700-level CS courses
facts.detail: For the exam subplans (Subplans 4 to 11), the 2026-2027 catalog says students must complete 18 credits of 700-level CS courses. There is no thesis or project to exclude. This matches the number in department-page fact f7 and also satisfies plan-of-study fact f16 (18 of 30 is more than 50 percent). The catalog therefore uses different 700-level minima by subplan: 12 excluding thesis (thesis and Integrated BS-MS), 15 excluding the project (project), and 18 (exam).
facts.quote: Students must complete 18 credits of 700-level CS courses.

facts.name: Exam subplans: 9-credit area list plus 21 other credits, up to 6 outside CS
facts.detail: Each exam subplan requires 9 credits from that subplan's required-course list plus 21 credits of other 600- or 700-level Computer Science courses, and students may complete up to 6 credits outside of CS. Outside credits must be related to computer applications and approved by the CS graduate committee. The 6-credit outside allowance is looser than the 3-credit outside cap on the thesis and project subplans (and on existing plan-of-study facts f11 and f14).
facts.quote: Complete 21 credits of 600- or 700- level Computer Science (CS) courses. Students may complete up to 6 credits outside of CS.

facts.name: Exam subplan must be declared before 19 CS credits
facts.detail: An exam subplan must be declared and approved before the student completes 19 credits of CS coursework.
facts.quote: Exam subplan must be declared and approved before completing 19 credits of CS coursework.

facts.name: Exam comprehensive oral exam, two attempts
facts.detail: On the exam subplans, students choose a specialized area covered by CS 600/700-level courses and approved by the graduate affairs committee, take 3 courses in that area, form a committee (one chair, two other departmental members, and one from outside), and take an oral exam on assigned papers or reading. Students have only two attempts to pass the comprehensive oral exam, and must pass a final comprehensive oral examination to graduate.
facts.quote: Students will have only two attempts to pass the comprehensive oral exam.

facts.name: In-program GPA and two-semester probation window (catalog)
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 catalog says a student's total GPA must be 3.00 or higher while in the program. If it falls below 3.00, the student is placed on academic probation and must have an overall GPA of at least 3.00 by the end of two subsequent semesters, or be separated from the graduate program. This conflicts with existing department-master's-page fact f10, whose detail said a student may be dropped if the GPA stays below 3.0 the next regular semester. The catalog wording ('two subsequent semesters') is kept alongside f10; no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: A student whose GPA falls below 3.00 will be placed on academic probation. That student must have an overall GPA of at least 3.00 by the end of two subsequent semesters; otherwise the student will be separated from the graduate program.
